governing: block shear of the bracket plate (AISC 360-22 J4.3), block of the top 2 bolt rows and both bolt columns: 44.11 kip demand against 45.51 kip allowable
notes: final.petra is identical to try3.petra, which Petra checked as PASS (15 of 15 obligations certified, ASD, service shear 0 to 88.107 kip at e = 6 in, no waivers, loads as given). Design: 5/16 in A572 Gr 50 bracket plate, 20.75 in deep (2.25 in top and bottom edge distance, 6 rows at 3.25 in pitch). Two bolt columns at 4 in gauge straddle the W12x65 web, with 1.25 in side edge distance. 12 bolts, 3/4 in A490-N (Group 150, threads included), snug-tightened in standard holes. Other utilisations: bolts 0.949 (elastic method, more conservative than the IC method), shear rupture 0.933, shear yield 0.679, plate lateral-torsional buckling (F11) 0.469, flexural rupture 0.423, flexural yield 0.35. The governing detailing check is edge distance at 0.80. My own hand check of tearout in the direction of each bolt's elastic force (J3.11) peaks at about 0.96 at the top bolt farthest from the load, against the 1.25 in side edge, so do not reduce plate_edge or substitute A325-N bolts. Petra does not check the following, and the engineer of record must: (1) The plate as drawn covers only the bolt region. It must extend to the load line 6 in from the bolt centroid, 4 in past the near bolt column, and the load must be delivered into the plate there. (2) The W12x65 column must carry the bracket's eccentric reaction, about 530 kip-in about its weak axis and 550 kip-in about its strong axis at service load. (3) The 4 in gauge is tighter than the usual 5-1/2 in gauge for this flange. It passes Petra's Manual Part 7 tightening clearance, and by my estimate the nuts and washers clear the web fillet, but confirm with the fabricator. (4) A490 bolts must not be galvanized. A snug-tightened bearing joint assumes static load.
